title: Discontinuities & Asymptotes
summary: Rational and related functions have discontinuities: removable holes (canceling factors) and infinite discontinuities (vertical asymptotes). End behavior gives horizontal or slant asymptotes. Understanding these previews limits in calculus.

vertical asymptote.plain: A line the graph races along to $\pm\infty$.

horizontal asymptote.plain: A far-out level the graph nears.

slant asymptote.in_class: Top degree one more than bottom.

concept_sections.heading: Removable vs infinite
concept_sections.explanation: A factor that cancels top and bottom leaves a hole (removable); a denominator zero that doesn't cancel gives a vertical asymptote (infinite).

concept_sections.heading: Vertical asymptotes
concept_sections.explanation: Near a vertical asymptote the function shoots to $+\infty$ or $-\infty$. Check the sign on each side to draw the branches.
math_steps: Test the sign on each side.

concept_sections.heading: Horizontal asymptotes
concept_sections.explanation: For large $|x|$, a rational function levels off according to the degree comparison — the horizontal asymptote (or none).
math_steps: Apply the rule ($0$, coefficient ratio, or none).

concept_sections.heading: Slant asymptotes
concept_sections.explanation: If the top's degree exceeds the bottom's by one, dividing gives a line the graph approaches diagonally.
math_steps: Divide to get the linear quotient.
That line is the slant asymptote.

concept_sections.heading: A preview of limits
concept_sections.explanation: These behaviors describe what a function approaches near a point or at infinity — exactly the idea of a limit, which calculus makes precise.
math_steps: Describe behavior near holes and asymptotes.
